'''Paulette Libermann''' (14 November 1919 – 10 July 2007) was a French mathematician who became a full professor at the [[University of Rennes]] in 1958. As a researcher, she specialized in [[differential geometry]]
and [[global analysis]], in particular [[G-structure on a manifold|G-structures]], [[Cartan's equivalence method]], and [[contact geometry]]. In 1987 she wrote together with [[Charles-Michel Marle]] one of the first textbooks on symplectic geometry and analytical mechanics.<ref name="aeh" /><ref group="pub" name=":0" />

In [[symplectic geometry]], the Libermann foliation is named after her.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-11 |title=72 women scientists, including 11 exceptional mathematicians, will soon be featured on the Eiffel Tower! {{!}} CNRS Mathématiques |url=https://www.insmi.cnrs.fr/en/cnrsinfo/72-femmes-scientifiques-dont-11-mathematiciennes-exception-bientot-sur-tour-eiffel |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=www.insmi.cnrs.fr |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Born on 14 November 1919 in Paris, Libermann was one of three sisters belonging to a family of Russian-Ukrainian [[Yiddish]]-speaking Jewish immigrants to France.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Libermann}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach|first=Yvette|title=Paulette Libermann|date=October 2007|url=https://smf.emath.fr/publications/la-gazette-des-mathematiciens-114-octobre-2007|work=La Gazette des mathématiciens|volume=114|pages=53–54|publisher=[[Société Mathématique de France]]|language=fr|author-link=Yvette Kosmann-Schwarzbach}}</ref> 

After attending the [[Lycée Lamartine]], she began her university studies in 1938 at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]], a college in [[Sèvres]] for training women to become school teachers. Due to the reforms of the new director [[Eugénie Cotton]], who wanted her school to be at the same level of [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]], Libermann was taught by leading mathematicians including [[Élie Cartan]], [[Jacqueline Ferrand]] and [[André Lichnerowicz]].<ref name="mactutor" /><ref name="yks">{{citation|last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach|first=Yvette|title=Women mathematicians in France in the mid-twentieth century|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17498430.2014.976804|journal=BSHM Bulletin: Journal of the British Society for the History of Mathematics|volume=30|issue=3|pages=227–242|year=2015|arxiv=1502.07597|bibcode=2015arXiv150207597K|doi=10.1080/17498430.2014.976804|s2cid=119148294|authorlink=Yvette Kosmann-Schwarzbach}}.</ref><ref name="cma">{{citation|last=Marles|first=Charles|title=Hommage à Paulette Libermann|date=October 2007|url=https://smf.emath.fr/publications/la-gazette-des-mathematiciens-114-octobre-2007|journal=La Gazette des mathématiciens|volume=114|pages=51–53|trans-title=Homage to Paulette Libermann|publisher=[[Société Mathématique de France]]|language=fr|author-link=Charles-Michel Marle}}</ref>

Two years later, upon completion of her studies, she was prevented from taking the [[agrégation]] and becoming a teacher because of the anti-Jewish laws instituted by the [[German military administration in occupied France during World War II|German occupation]]. However, thanks to a scholarship provided by Cotton, she began doing research under Cartan's supervision.<ref name="mactutor" /><ref name="cma" />

In 1942, she and her family escaped Paris for [[Lyon]], where they hid from the persecutions by [[Klaus Barbie]] for two years.<ref name="mactutor" /> After the [[liberation of Paris]] in 1944, she returned to Sèvres and completed her studies, obtaining the agrégation.<ref name="yks" /><ref name="cma" /> From 1945 to 1947, she studied at [[Oxford University]].<ref name="asc"/>

=== Career ===
Libermann taught briefly in a school at [[Douai]], and then got a scholarship to study at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] between 1945 and 1947, where she obtained a bachelor's degree under the supervision of [[J. H. C. Whitehead]].<ref name="yks" />

From 1947 to 1951 she held a teaching position at a school for girls in [[Strasbourg]]. However, at the encouragement of Élie Cartan, during this period she also continued her research at [[Louis Pasteur University|Université Louis Pasteur]] under the leadership of [[Charles Ehresmann]].<ref name="yks" /> Together with Ehresmann, she published a number of papers.<ref name="asc"/>
	
In 1951 she left teaching for a research position at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]], and in 1953 she completed her doctoral thesis, entitled ''Sur le problème d’équivalence de certaines structures infinitésimales'' [On the equivalence problem of certain infinitesimal structures], under the supervision of [[Charles Ehresmann]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=96186}}</ref><ref name="mactutor" /> The thesis documents her investigation of foliations of [[symplectic manifold]]s and defined what would later be known as the affine structure of a [[Lagrangian foliation]].<ref name="asc"/> 

After her PhD, Libermann was appointed assistant professor at the [[University of Rennes]] in 1954 and full professor at the same university in 1958.<ref name="yks" /> The university's maths department was different in 1960 because it had a relatively high percentage of women. There were fifteen professors and three of them were women. Libermann was one of them and the other two were [[Marie Charpentier]] and [[Huguette Delavault]]. Charpentier taught mechanics and Huguette Delavault was to be known for championing the role of women.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trois mathématiciennes à Rennes en 1960 |url=https://www.echosciences-paysdelaloire.fr/articles/trois-mathematiciennes-a-rennes-en-1960 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=www.echosciences-paysdelaloire.fr}}</ref>

In 1966 Libermann moved to the [[University of Paris]], becoming one of the first few women to receive a full professorship in a French university, and when the university split in 1968, she joined [[Paris Diderot University]], from which she retired in 1986.<ref name="yks" /><ref name="cma" />

== Research ==
Libermann's research involved many different aspects of [[differential geometry]] and [[global analysis]].<ref name="mactutor" /><ref>{{citation|last=Chaperon|first=Marc|title=Souvenirs de Paulette Libermann: Un portrait mathématique de Paulette Libermann (1919-2007)|date=November 8, 2009|url=http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Souvenirs-de-Paulette-Libermann.html|publisher=CNRS|language=French|access-date=May 17, 2015|archive-date=May 19, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519144538/http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Souvenirs-de-Paulette-Libermann.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="aeh">{{citation|last=Ehresmann|first=Andrée C.|title=Sur Paulette Libermann (1919-2007)|date=2007|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CTGDC_2007__48_4_270_0|journal=Cahiers de Topologie et Géométrie Différentielle Catégoriques|volume=48|issue=4|pages=270–274|trans-title=On Paulette Libermann (1919-2007)|language=fr|mr=2394014|zbl=1137.01317|author-link=Andrée Ehresmann|via={{Interlanguage link|Numérisation de documents anciens mathématiques.|lt=Numérisation de documents anciens mathématiques.|fr}}}}.</ref> In particular, she worked on [[G-structure on a manifold|G-structures]] and [[Cartan's equivalence method]],<ref group="pub">{{citation|last=Libermann|first=Paulette|date=1954-12-01|title=Sur le problème d'équivalence de certaines structures infinitésimales|journal=Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata|language=fr|volume=36|issue=1|pages=27–120|doi=10.1007/BF02412833|s2cid=120658595|issn=1618-1891|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Lie groupoid|Lie groupoids]] and [[Pseudogroup|Lie pseudogroups]],<ref group="pub">{{citation|last=Libermann|first=Paulette|title=Pseudogroupes infinitésimaux attachés aux pseudogroupes de Lie|date=1959|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=BSMF_1959__87__409_0|journal=Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France|volume=87|pages=409–425|language=fr|doi=10.24033/bsmf.1536|doi-access=free}}</ref> higher-order [[Connection (mathematics)|connections]],<ref group="pub">{{citation|last=Libermann|first=Paulette|title=Sur la géométrie des prolongements des espaces fibrés vectoriels|date=1964|url=https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/AIF_1964__14_1_145_0/|journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier|volume=14|issue=1|pages=145–172|doi=10.5802/aif.167|issn=1777-5310|doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[contact geometry]].<ref group="pub">{{citation|last=Libermann|first=Paulette|title=Legendre foliations on contact manifolds|date=1991-06-01|journal=Differential Geometry and Its Applications|volume=1|issue=1|pages=57–76|language=en|doi=10.1016/0926-2245(91)90022-2|issn=0926-2245|doi-access=}}</ref>

After her appointment as a full professor in Paris. Libermann continued her work as an influential researcher, developing the work of Cartan and Ehlermann and publishing some 70 papers until her death in 2007.<ref name="asc"/>

In 1987, together with [[Charles-Michel Marle]], she wrote one of the first textbooks on [[symplectic geometry]] and [[analytical mechanics]].<ref name="asc">{{citation|last=Riddle|first=Larry|title=Paulette Libermann|url=http://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/libermann.htm|work=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|accessdate=2015-05-16}}.</ref><ref group="pub" name=":0">{{citation|last1=Libermann|first1=Paulette|title=Symplectic Geometry and Analytical Mechanics|date=1987|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-009-3807-6|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-94-009-3807-6|last2=Marle|first2=Charles-Michel|isbn=978-90-277-2439-7|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Libermann travelled widely, speaking at many conferences and visiting universities and research associations, including Oxford University, the [[University of California at Berkeley]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] and the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|National Institute of Pure and Applied Mathematics]] in Brazil.<ref name="asc"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Libermann/|title=Paulette Libermann|author=O'Connor, J.J.; Robertso, E.F.|publisher=MacTutor|date=December 2021|access-date=13 July 2026}}</ref>

==Honors==
In 2026, Libermann was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by Isabelle Vauglin of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-09 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-09</ref>
